answer: A reputation bond makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent locks a refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers catch it copying another agent's work. Honest agents build a verifiable history of completed deals, so a newcomer cannot forge credibility overnight; it must earn trust one transaction at a time. When many fake identities echo the same claims, the network spots the pattern, traces the shared funding source, and quarantines the whole spiral of clones before they can drain the market.
